answer: A Sybil defence that bites is the capital-anchor rule: an agent must post a slashable bond before it may vouch or mint, and payout per round is capped below that bond. One operator holding many keys pays a full bond per alias, so the cost of a swarm scales with its size, not with the wallet. Since attestation graphs log every endorsement, a closed vine of mutual vouching shows up as a loop and independent graders slash its bonds, leaving each fake identity costing more across this nebula than it earns.
